q: At what age is orchidopexy ideally performed?
What happens with traction on the spermatic cord under light anaesthesia?
why: A vagal response; deepen anaesthesia before cord traction and have atropine drawn up.

q: Which block is an alternative to a caudal for orchidopexy?
why: Ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric block covers the groin incision.

q: What is the RCoA lower age limit generally used for paediatric day surgery?
why: Ex-premature babies under 60 weeks PCA carry an apnoea risk.

q: Which social factor makes day case less suitable?
o: Living more than 1 hour from hospital or no telephone or transport
why: Also poor housing or a carer unable to cope.

q: What fasting time applies to formula milk in children?
why: Solids and formula 6 hours, breast milk 4 hours, clear fluids up to 1 hour.

q: What volume limit is suggested for clear fluids up to 1 hour before induction?
why: Clear fluids up to 1 hour, to a maximum of 3 ml/kg.

q: Which surgical complication is delayed after orchidopexy?
why: Also re-ascent of the testis and wound infection.

q: What does "D" in the paediatric BINDS history stand for?
Delay in gross motor milestones in a boy could indicate which risk at anaesthesia?
o: Anaesthesia-induced rhabdomyolysis from an undiagnosed myopathy such as Duchenne
why: Use TIVA and avoid suxamethonium where AIR risk is suspected.
